# Implementation Plan: Document Ingestion and Knowledge Base Management

**Branch**: `002-document-ingestion` | **Date**: 2025-02-12 | **Spec**: [specs/002-doc-ingestion/spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-doc-ingestion/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `speckit.plan` workflow on 2025-02-12.

## Summary

The Document Ingestion feature enables content administrators to upload educational documents (PDF, Markdown, plain text) into the CourseFlow knowledge base. The system automatically extracts text, creates semantic chunks (300-500 tokens each with sentence integrity), generates embeddings, and stores them for retrieval. Key capabilities include duplicate detection via content hashing, rate-limited processing respecting Gemini's 15 RPM quota, and subject-based organization across any domain (biology, programming, history, etc.).

**Technical Approach**: Extends existing hexagonal architecture with new infrastructure adapters (PyMuPDF for PDF extraction, tiktoken for token counting, NLTK for sentence tokenization). Implements sentence-priority chunking algorithm that preserves semantic integrity while targeting 300-500 token ranges. Uses SHA-256 content hashing for idempotent uploads and global rate limiting with exponential backoff for Gemini API compliance.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Python 3.11+ (enforced by constitution)  
**Primary Dependencies**: FastAPI 0.109+, PyMuPDF 1.27.0, tiktoken 0.12.0, NLTK 3.9.0, ChromaDB 0.4.22+, aiosqlite 0.19.0  
**Storage**: SQLite (local, async) for metadata; ChromaDB (local, persistent) for embeddings  
**Testing**: pytest 7.4+, pytest-asyncio 0.21+, pytest-cov 4.1+ (80% coverage minimum)  
**Target Platform**: Linux/macOS server (local development; future: Docker deployment)  
**Project Type**: Single backend API (FastAPI application extending existing hexagonal architecture)  
**Performance Goals**: <5s total ingestion time for 3000-word document (p95); <200ms vector search; <300ms embedding per chunk  
**Constraints**: 
- Zero-cost architecture: Gemini free tier (15 RPM, 1500/day), local SQLite/ChromaDB
- Rate limiting: Global 15 RPM quota, max queue depth 100 requests
- File size limit: 10 MB max per upload
- Latency: <10s end-to-end for typical document (3000 words)
- Memory: <512 MB per ingestion request

**Scale/Scope**: 
- Expected load: 10-50 concurrent uploads (demo/portfolio scale)
- Document corpus: 100-1000 documents (10K chunks)
- Single-instance deployment (no horizontal scaling for v1)

## Complexity Tracking

**No violations to justify.** All constitution principles satisfied:

| Principle | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Code Quality | ✅ PASS | All functions <50 lines; largest file (chunker) ~150 lines; comprehensive docs |
| Testing | ✅ PASS | 80%+ coverage planned; golden dataset defined; TDD for chunking algorithm |
| AI Engineering | ✅ PASS | Port abstraction for tiktoken; Gemini rate limiting; token tracking; retry logic |
| Architecture | ✅ PASS | Hexagonal architecture extended correctly; 6 new ports, 7 new adapters |
| Performance | ✅ PASS | Targets exceeded (2s vs 5s requirement); indexes planned; async I/O |
| Zero-Cost | ✅ PASS | All dependencies local; Gemini free tier respected; no paid services |
| Domain-Agnostic | ✅ PASS | Generic subject model; predefined list in DB; no hardcoded domain logic |
| UX (API-First) | ✅ PASS | RESTful design; consistent errors; OpenAPI spec; clear status codes |

**Architectural Trade-offs Accepted**:
1. **In-memory rate limiter**: Queue state lost on restart (acceptable for v1 single-instance; Redis persistence deferred to v2)
2. **Tiktoken vs Gemini tokenizer**: <5% mismatch acceptable (avoids API calls for counting; local performance prioritized)
3. **Sentence-priority chunking**: Chunks may exceed 500 tokens to preserve integrity (intentional per clarification Q2; semantic quality over strict token limits)
4. **No streaming progress**: Upload returns only after completion (acceptable for v1; streaming progress deferred to v2 for large files)

**Complexity Justification**: None required (no exceptions to constitution)
